'''Dame Patricia Rose Bergquist''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|DBE}} (née '''Smyth''', 10 March 1933 – 9 September 2009) was a New Zealand zoologist who specialised in [[anatomy]] and [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]]. At the time of her death, she was professor emerita of zoology and honorary professor of anatomy with radiology at the [[University of Auckland]].

==Early life, family and education==
Born Patricia Rose Smyth in the [[Auckland]] suburb of [[Devonport, New Zealand|Devonport]] on 10 March 1933, Bergquist was the daughter of William Smyth, an electrician, and Bertha Ellen ({{nee}} Penny) Smyth, a homemaker. She had a younger brother Norman and a sister Catherine.<ref name="RSNZ obituary">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/obituaries/fellows-obituaries/patricia-rose-bergquist/ |title=Patricia Rose Bergquist (1933–2009) |last=Nicholson |first=Louise F.B. |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand | access-date=11 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/AS19330313.2.2 |title=Births |date=13 March 1933 |work=[[Auckland Star]] |access-date=11 May 2019 |page=1}}</ref> 

She was educated at Devonport Primary School, and then [[Takapuna Grammar School]] where she was [[Dux#Education|dux]] in her final year.<ref name="RSNZ obituary"/> She then began studying at [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]] in 1950, graduating [[Master of Science|MSc]] with first-class honours in botany in 1956; the title of her master's thesis was ''Contributions to the study of the loxsomaceae''.<ref name="RSNZ obituary"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://catalogue.library.auckland.ac.nz/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=uoa_alma21159778950002091&context=L&vid=NEWUI&search_scope=Combined_Local&tab=books&lang=en_US |title=Contributions to the study of the loxsomaceae |year=1956 |publisher=Auckland University College |first=Patricia Rose |last=Smyth |access-date=11 May 2019}}</ref> After completing a second MSc equivalent in zoology, she undertook doctoral studies at Auckland, obtaining her [[PhD]], supervised by [[William Roy McGregor]] and [[John Morton (zoologist)|John Morton]], on the taxonomy of the [[Porifera]] in 1961.<ref name="RSNZ obituary"/><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Bergquist |first=Patricia |year=1961 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=The Demospongiae of New Zealand-Systematics, distribution and relationships |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |hdl=2292/2189 |url=https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/handle/2292/2189}}</ref> Bergquist was the first person to earn a doctoral degree in zoology from the University of Auckland.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/1968-2017/patricia-bergquist/|title=Patricia Bergquist|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi|access-date=2019-08-13}}</ref>

In 1958, she married Peter Bergquist, a noted molecular biologist, and the couple went on to have one daughter.<ref name="RSNZ obituary"/><ref name="Peter ONZM">{{cite web |url=https://gg.govt.nz/file/18338 |title=Peter Bergquist |date=29 August 2012 |publisher=Office of the Governor-General |access-date=11 May 2019}}</ref>

==Academic and research career==
Following her doctorate, Patricia Bergquist studied overseas, initially at [[Yale University]] where she broadened her systematic expertise, before returning to New Zealand and becoming an educator and researcher at the [[University of Auckland]] on matters related to anatomy, taxonomy and zoology, with particular interest in the [[sea sponge|marine sponge]]. She felt a stable framework of higher level classification which would permit recognition of generic relationships and facilitate descriptions of new species was missing.<ref name="RSNZ obituary"/> When Bergquist received a Personal Chair at the University of Auckland, she was the first woman at that university to do so.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tiaki.natlib.govt.nz/#details=ethesaurus.134348|title=ATL: Unpublished Collections|website=tiaki.natlib.govt.nz|access-date=2019-08-13}}</ref>

She co-authored (with Mary E. Sinclair) ''The Morphology and Behaviour of Larvae of Some Intertidal Sponges'' for the ''New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research'', which was published on 20 October 1967.

Bergquist's notable students include [[Michelle Kelly (marine scientist)|Michelle Kelly-Borges]] and [[Jane Fromont]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Kelly-Borges |first=Michelle |year=1991 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=The Order Hadromerida (Porifera: Demospongiae), taxonomy and relationships of the major families |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |hdl=2292/1994 |url=https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/handle/2292/1994}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite Q|Q111050301}}</ref>

In 1979, Bergquist was conferred the degree of [[Doctor of Science]] by the University of Auckland, on the basis of 28 submitted publications.<ref name="HBTQ"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Publications submitted for the degree of D.Sc. |last=Bergquist |first=Patricia R. |url=https://catalogue.library.auckland.ac.nz/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=uoa_alma21159311420002091&context=L&vid=NEWUI&search_scope=Combined_Local&tab=books&lang=en_US |year=1979 |publisher=[[University of Auckland]] |access-date=11 May 2019}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Bergquist was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1982,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/a-c/ |title=List of all Fellows with surnames A–C |year=2017 |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=11 May 2019}}</ref> and in 1989 she was awarded the [[Hector Memorial Medal]] by the Royal Society of New Zealand.<ref name="HBTQ">{{cite book |last1=Taylor |first1=Alister |last2=Coddington |first2=Deborah |author-link1=Alister Taylor |author-link2=Deborah Coddington |title=Honoured by the Queen – New Zealand |year=1994 |publisher=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa |location=Auckland |isbn=0-908578-34-2 |page=65}}</ref> In the [[1994 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|1994 New Year Honours]], she was appointed a [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]], for services to science.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=53528 |date=31 December 1993 |page=33 |supp=2}}</ref> Her husband, Peter Bergquist, was appointed an [[Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to science, in the [[2012 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|2012 Queen's Birthday and Diamond Jubilee Honours]].<ref name="Peter ONZM"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dpmc.govt.nz/publications/queens-birthday-and-diamond-jubilee-honours-list-2012 |title=Queen's Birthday and Diamond Jubilee honours list 2012 |date=4 June 2012 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=11 May 2019}}</ref>

==Legacy==
Numerous sponges have been named in her honour, e.g., ''[[Xestospongia bergquistia]]''  <small>Fromont, 1991</small>, ''[[Tethya bergquistae]]'' <small>Hooper, 1994,</small><ref>{{Cite web |last=Atlas of Living Australia |title=Species: ''Tethya bergquistae'' |url=https://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:afd.taxon:dc7b9d6d-38b5-41f5-87a9-8b766ebeb181 |access-date=2022-03-04 |website=bie.ala.org.au |language=en-AU}}</ref> ''[[Acarnus bergquistae]]'' <small>Van Soest, Hooper & Hiemstra, 1991</small>,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Atlas of Living Australia |title=Species: ''Acarnus bergquistae'' |url=https://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:afd.taxon:fdefc922-3187-496b-8655-8ddb8eb72fc1 |access-date=2022-03-04 |website=bie.ala.org.au |language=en-AU}}</ref> ''[[Plakortis bergquistae]]'' <small>Muricy, 2011,</small><ref>{{cite web|url=https://biodiversity.org.au/afd/taxa/Plakortis_bergquistae|title= Australian Faunal Directory: ''Plakortis bergquistae''|website=biodiversity.org.au|accessdate=2022-03-05}}</ref> and ''[[Phyllospongia bergquistae]]'' <small>Wahab & Fromont, 2020</small>.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q110667756}}</ref>

Bergquist featured as one of the Royal Society Te Apārangi's "[[150 women in 150 words]]" project in 2017.<ref name=":0" />

==Death==
Patricia Bergquist died of [[breast cancer]] in Auckland on 9 September 2009, aged 76.<ref name="RSNZ obituary"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Patricia Bergquist death notice |date=11 September 2009 |work= [[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref>
